observations.content: Assistant concluded prior probe was actually ~180k tokens not 247k (their tokenizer counts ~5.5 chars/token; assistant's /4-char estimate overestimated), so the 200k ceiling was never hit.

Assistant found cached_tokens=0 across all 3 calls sharing an identical 180k prefix, concluding the zaicp plan endpoint has no prompt caching through the gateway, which roughly doubles high-context cost vs earlier simulation.

Assistant ran extended probe with N=1850 filler blocks via /tmp/probe2.json, model zaicp/glm-5.3, targeting ~255k real tokens, single call asking head magic word, last block number, and middle access code.
Probe 2 result: billed 256,903 prompt tokens, filler chars 1,375,631; reply recalled MAGIC-START-9C2B, block 1849, NEEDLE-MID-555, all replies start PINECONE.

Assistant determined zaicp is a Z.ai coding plan subscription quota (not pay-per-token; $1.40/M in models.json is only for cost tracking), and no-cache means quota burns at full input rate, reframing the cost debate as quota usage ~+45%/session at 250k vs 150k.

Assistant final verdict: keep compactAtContextTokens at 250k (verified safe to 257k+, quality perfect, instruction holds); drop to 200k only if user confirms they hit weekly quota limits; 300k+ and 500-700k rejected as unneeded/unverified.

Assistant explained safe threshold formula: threshold = model window minus ~55-65k, accounting for intra-turn tool growth +40k worst case, system+tools+reminders +15k, observer-wait delay adding one turn, and output budget +8-16k; recommended 140-150k for 200k-window models, 210-220k (round 200k) for 272k GPT, 250k for 1M GLM.

Assistant warned compactAtContextTokens is a single shared value for the whole workspace via .pi/settings.json (not per-model), so adding a GPT 272k agent to the same workspace forces lowering the shared threshold to 200k; OM does not support per-agent thresholds; must split workspace or use per-agent config.
User asked to revert to 150k, asked whether settings are done and if anything remains, and asked to use URL https://opnxng.com/ for searxng and report test results.

Assistant wrote compactAtContextTokens=150000 to /home/coder/workspaces/learn/.pi/settings.json and searxngBaseUrl=https://opnxng.com to /home/coder/.pi/web-search.json (which already had exaApiKey, jinaApiKey, fetchRouting); both writes succeeded.
web_search with provider searxng returned error 'SearXNG base URL is invalid or missing' because the tool loaded config at process start and does not see the newly written config until restart.

Direct curl tests of opnxng.com showed /search returns HTTP 429 Too Many Requests consistently (multiple UAs and waits up to 30s) while /config returns HTTP 200 JSON; assistant concluded the machine's shared cloud egress IP is rate-limited by the instance, not a config error.

Assistant reported settings officially done: roles 5 models + thinking pins, OM knobs at defaults with compactAt back to 150k, ask_question 300s already loaded, packages dedupe + proxy reasoning_split + searxng URL done, new OM report (status+timeline) running; next restart loads 150k and searxng config.

Assistant listed remaining non-settings items: Paseo zombie bug tracked via upstream PRs #3848/#3849 (STOP as golden rule when spinner hangs), optional A/B consolidator glm-5.3-flash saving ~$0.13/session, and optional drafting 2-3 unreported pi/Paseo bugs.
User asked assistant to research searx.space, searx.neocities.org, and searloc.org to find a high-uptime low-response SearXNG server as a fallback in case Exa fails.
Assistant fetched searx.space/data/instances.json into /tmp/instances.json and inspected structure (http.status_code, timing.search.all.median, uptime.uptimeMonth, comments at top level).

Filtering searx.space instances by status 200, uptimeMonth>=95%, success>=90% and sorting by uptime then latency gave top candidates: searxng.site (100%, 217ms), searxng.website (100%, 301ms), search.yuri.llc (100%, 335ms), search.ctq.ro (100%, 337ms), paulgo.io (100%, 382ms), searx.linxx.net (100%, 395ms), searxng.deggo.fyi (99.7%, 203ms), searx.tiekoetter.com (99.9%, 187ms fastest).

Direct curl tests of top 7 instances from this machine all failed: searxng.site 403, searx.tiekoetter.com 429, searxng.deggo.fyi 418, searxng.website 403, search.yuri.llc 429, paulgo.io 429, searx.linxx.net 403; assistant noted 403 means JSON disabled for public, 429 rate-limit on shared IP, 418 deliberate bot blocking, and concluded public SearXNG instances generally restrict JSON API to admins and block datacenter IPs.

Assistant attempted to inspect ~/.pi/agent/npm/node_modules/pi-web-access dist source to determine whether the searxng provider requests format=json or scrapes HTML, but grep produced no output (path pattern found nothing).
